title: Scalable Multi-Facility Workflows for Artificial Intelligence Applications in Climate Research
problem: Processing and analyzing vast, multi-modal earth observation satellite and earth system model datasets at scale poses challenges in data movement, preprocessing coordination, and AI inferencing across diverse computational resources.
motivation: Climate and environmental research requires efficient extraction of scientific insights from petascale satellite data through coordinated distributed AI processing across research facilities.
method: An automated multi-facility workflow orchestrates data collection, preprocessing, AI inferencing, and data movement across diverse computational resources at OLCF's Advanced Computing Ecosystem Testbed. The system seamlessly integrates research facilities managed by different federal agencies and performs dynamic tokenization and sharding of satellite data for distributed processing across multiple nodes with 80 workers.
key_novelty: Seamless orchestration of scientific workflows across multiple research facilities managed by different federal agencies to enable petascale coordinated climate data processing.
contributions: Multi-facility workflow system integrating facilities managed by different federal agencies
High-throughput processing of 12,000 satellite images in 44 seconds using 80 workers across 10 nodes
Dynamic tokenization and sharding approach for distributed AI model training on petascale satellite data
Scalable and efficient workflow execution across varying workloads in multi-facility environments

metrics.speedup: significantly reduces processing time versus single-facility baseline (exact value not specified)
metrics.other: maintains efficiency across varying workloads with thousands of GPUs

limitations: Specific baseline system comparisons, network latency overhead analysis, and inter-facility communication costs not discussed.
primary_theme: multi-facility workflow orchestration for climate data processing
